subject: TCO snapshot & next actions — batching, cache, budget constraints
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@swiftpay.com>
Cc: Rajiv Singh <rajiv.singh@swiftpay.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call TCO snapshot + batching/cache levers — next actions

Hi Elena,

Thanks again for taking time earlier — really helpful to walk through SwiftPay's current flow and constraints. Quick recap from my side and suggested next steps so we can move to a short pilot that demonstrates unit-economics improvements.

What we heard (pain points / goals)
- Volume & cost profile: ~500k authorization-like events/month; current ML calls are made for ~0.6 of those events on average (rules + model fallback), so ~300k model calls/month.
- Token footprint: median request ~420 tokens, response ~160 tokens (roughly 580 tokens per call).
- Budget constraint: finance cited a hard ceiling of ~$25k/month for inference at pilot scale; current spend is ~38–45k/month (various vendors + infra).
- Latency: product goal is 95th < 350 ms; some endpoints need sub-200ms.
- Reliability / compliance: must avoid PII leakage and need audit logs for decisioning.

What we propose for a pilot (scope & success criteria)
- Duration: 4 weeks (2-week ramp + 2-week measurement).
- Traffic: mirror a 1% slice of production traffic (sample provided, attached).
- Baseline & target: demonstrate >=40% reduction in per-call token cost through batching + KV/prefix caching and a model-variant swap; maintain 95th latency < 350 ms.
- Deliverables: cost delta report (tokens/$ and total monthlyized cost for projected production), latency profile, and a short runbook with safe-fallback policy.

Key levers we'll test
1) Batching: continuous batching at the router with target batch windows tuned to keep tail latency within SLOs; expected 20–30% token-time savings for throughputable endpoints.
2) KV/prefix caching: cache common prompt prefixes and deterministic lookups to avoid repeated token generation — expected 15–25% token savings for your workload patterns.
3) Model selection & quantization: run a small eval between a 7B dense variant and an 8-bit quantized 13B to trade accuracy vs. raw token cost.

Immediate asks / next steps
- Elena / Rajiv: confirm the $25k/month pilot constraint is the ceiling for this evaluation and that security can share any must-have controls (audit log format, KMS requirement).
- SwiftPay: share a sanitized sample of API traffic (attached CSV is a suggested template).
- Redwood (me + Karthik): we will produce a short TCO model and a pilot SOW by Wed 10/7.
- Schedule: propose kickoff week of 10/11.

Attachments: swiftpay-pilot-scope-v1.pdf (scope + SOW draft), sample-traffic-stats.csv (template).

If that all sounds right I'll get the SOW and a preliminary cost model over to you tomorrow.

Cheers,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com | (415) 555-0132

From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@swiftpay.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajiv Singh <rajiv.singh@swiftpay.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call TCO snapshot + batching/cache levers — next actions

Jonas — thanks for the thorough recap. Quick confirmations from our side:

- Budget: yes, $25k/month is the upper bound for anything we run under this evaluation budget line. Finance will not sign off higher without a clear payback within 60 days post-pilot.
- Latency: product emphasized 95th < 350 ms as the critical SLO; anything above that will need a fallback to a simpler rule-based path.
- Security: we'll need KMS integration and audit log schema; I copied Rajiv so his team can confirm any additional constraints.

We'll attach a sanitized sample later today — do not include any PII in the sample. Also please include a quick ROI table in the SOW that projects production monthly spend at 100% traffic with and without the proposed levers.

Happy to kick off week of 10/11 — Rajiv, can you confirm if security can review scope by 10/9?

Thanks,
Elena
Director, Product Ops — SwiftPay
elena.morales@swiftpay.com
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Morales <elena.morales@swiftpay.com>, Rajiv Singh <rajiv.singh@swiftpay.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Post-call TCO snapshot + batching/cache levers — next actions

Marissa / Karthik — looping you both in to align on responsibilities and immediate deliverables (Elena confirmed budget ceiling and security review timeline). Below are our initial internal asks: 

Action items (owner / ETA)
- Karthik: build a short TCO model (spreadsheet) that takes SwiftPay inputs and shows baseline vs. lever-based scenarios (batching, cache, quantized model). ETA: Wed 10/7 COB. Attach a column with projected payback days at production scale.
- Marissa: draft a concise SOW (1–2 pages) that includes the 4-week pilot, success criteria, deliverables, and $25k budget ceiling note for finance. ETA: Wed 10/7 EOD.
- Jonas: coordinate kickoff scheduling and share preliminary runbook for safe fallback and latency guards. ETA: Fri 10/9.

Notes / constraints to keep in mind
- The sample traffic indicates a high proportion of short prompts (~<100 tokens) and a long tail of 1–2% very long prompts. We should propose a hybrid policy (cache + bypass rules) to avoid tail latency regressions.
- Security: assume KMS for any keying, and that audit logs need to be exportable in CSV/JSON for their SIEM. Karthik — please prepare a one-paragraph note on what Redwood can and cannot provide out-of-the-box.

I'll draft the ROI table template for Marissa and Karthik to fill; plan to share the combined packet to Elena by Wed 10/7.

Thanks — quick turnaround on this will be important so they can get sign-off before 10/11.

Jonas
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
